The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:

  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/rbf-available-ns-retry.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: rbf-available-ns-retry" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/rbf-available-ns-retry.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/rbf-available-ns-retry.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):
{"slug":"rbf-available-ns-retry","status":"done"|"partial"|"blocked","files":["..."],"committed":true|false,"patch_bytes":<int>,"summary":"<=3 sentences on what you changed","notes":"anything the orchestrator must know (conflicts, follow-ups, uncertainty)"}

1	title: 'HDFS-16359. RBF: RouterRpcServer#invokeAtAvailableNs does not take effect when retrying'
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  In Router-based federation, a multi-destination mount should keep working when one target namespace fails and another namespace is still available. Today invokeAtAvailableNs can lose that retry behavior because it rebuilds the candidate set incorrectly during retries.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Make RouterRpcServer#invokeAtAvailableNs retry against the remaining available namespaces after one namespace has already failed, instead of effectively discarding the fallback set. This should restore the intended high-availability behavior for multi-destination mounts.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  If the first namespace chosen for a multi-destination operation fails, the router retries the operation on another available namespace and can still return a successful result when an alternate namespace is healthy.
16	
17	  '
18

<T> T invokeAtAvailableNs(RemoteMethod method, Class<T> clazz)
      throws IOException {
    String nsId = subclusterResolver.getDefaultNamespace();
    // If default Ns is not present return result from first namespace.
    Set<FederationNamespaceInfo> nss = namenodeResolver.getNamespaces();
    try {
      if (!nsId.isEmpty()) {
        return rpcClient.invokeSingle(nsId, method, clazz);
      }
      // If no namespace is available, throw IOException.
      IOException io = new IOException("No namespace available.");
      return invokeOnNs(method, clazz, io, nss);
    } catch (IOException ioe) {
      if (!clientProto.isUnavailableSubclusterException(ioe)) {
        LOG.debug("{} exception cannot be retried",
            ioe.getClass().getSimpleName());
        throw ioe;
      }
      Set<FederationNamespaceInfo> nssWithoutFailed = getNameSpaceInfo(nsId);
      return invokeOnNs(method, clazz, ioe, nssWithoutFailed);
    }
  }

  /**
   * Invoke the method on first available namespace,
   * throw no namespace available exception, if no namespaces are available.
   * @param method the remote method.
   * @param clazz  Class for the return type.
   * @param ioe    IOException .
   * @param nss    List of name spaces in the federation
   * @return the response received after invoking method.
   * @throws IOException
   */
  <T> T invokeOnNs(RemoteMethod method, Class<T> clazz, IOException ioe,
      Set<FederationNamespaceInfo> nss) throws IOException {
    if (nss.isEmpty()) {
      throw ioe;
    }
    String nsId = nss.iterator().next().getNameserviceId();
    return rpcClient.invokeSingle(nsId, method, clazz);
  }

  /**
   * Get set of namespace info's removing the already invoked namespaceinfo.
   * @param nsId already invoked namespace id
   * @return List of name spaces in the federation on
   * removing the already invoked namespaceinfo.
   */
  private Set<FederationNamespaceInfo> getNameSpaceInfo(String nsId) {
    Set<FederationNamespaceInfo> namespaceInfos = new HashSet<>();
    for (FederationNamespaceInfo ns : namespaceInfos) {
      if (!nsId.equals(ns.getNameserviceId())) {
        namespaceInfos.add(ns);
      }
    }
    return namespaceInfos;
  }

<T> T invokeAtAvailableNs(RemoteMethod method, Class<T> clazz)
      throws IOException {
    String nsId = subclusterResolver.getDefaultNamespace();
    // If default Ns is not present return result from first namespace.
    Set<FederationNamespaceInfo> nss = namenodeResolver.getNamespaces();
    // If no namespace is available, throw IOException.
    IOException io = new IOException("No namespace available.");
    try {
      if (!nsId.isEmpty()) {
        return rpcClient.invokeSingle(nsId, method, clazz);
      }
      return invokeOnNs(method, clazz, io, nss);
    } catch (IOException ioe) {
      if (!clientProto.isUnavailableSubclusterException(ioe)) {
        LOG.debug("{} exception cannot be retried",
            ioe.getClass().getSimpleName());
        throw ioe;
      }
      // Remove the already tried namespace.
      nss.removeIf(n -> n.getNameserviceId().equals(nsId));
      return invokeOnNs(method, clazz, ioe, nss);
    }
  }

  /**
   * Invoke the method sequentially on available namespaces,
   * throw no namespace available exception, if no namespaces are available.
   * @param method the remote method.
   * @param clazz  Class for the return type.
   * @param ioe    IOException .
   * @param nss    List of name spaces in the federation
   * @return the response received after invoking method.
   * @throws IOException
   */
  <T> T invokeOnNs(RemoteMethod method, Class<T> clazz, IOException ioe,
      Set<FederationNamespaceInfo> nss) throws IOException {
    if (nss.isEmpty()) {
      throw ioe;
    }
    for (FederationNamespaceInfo fnInfo : nss) {
      String nsId = fnInfo.getNameserviceId();
      LOG.debug("Invoking {} on namespace {}", method, nsId);
      try {
        return rpcClient.invokeSingle(nsId, method, clazz);
      } catch (IOException e) {
        LOG.debug("Failed to invoke {} on namespace {}", method, nsId, e);
        // Ignore the exception and try on other namespace, if the tried
        // namespace is unavailable, else throw the received exception.
        if (!clientProto.isUnavailableSubclusterException(e)) {
          throw e;
        }
      }
    }
    // Couldn't successfully invoke on any namespace, throw the ioe.
    throw ioe;
  }
